title: The use of Peres lattices in periodically driven systems
authors: Lukáš Honsa, Jan Střeleček, Jakub Novotný, Pavel Cejnar
abstract: We demonstrate the strength of the method of Peres lattices in periodically driven quantum systems. The method, which has previously been used mostly in stationary systems, enables us to efficiently detect resonances in the driven system, to monitor the onset of chaos, and to recognize critical properties of the Floquet modes. It also allows quick comparisons of the spectra of Floquet modes for various driving Hamiltonians and transparent tests of the iterative approximation techniques based on effective stationary Hamiltonians.
summary: This work extends the Peres lattice technique from stationary Hamiltonians to periodically driven quantum systems. It demonstrates that this method is highly effective for diagnosing complex dynamics, allowing researchers to map out resonances, track the onset of chaos, and identify critical points in Floquet spectra. The analysis confirms the utility of geometric tools to understand time-dependent many-body physics.
main_problem: The primary goal is extending the Peres lattice method, originally for stationary systems, to analyze complex dynamics in periodically driven quantum systems.
main_result: The Peres lattice successfully diagnoses key features of driven systems, including detecting resonances, monitoring the onset of chaos, and characterizing critical points related to Floquet modes.
method: The analysis involves mapping the time-periodic evolution onto an extended, effective stationary Hamiltonian whose eigenstates (Floquet modes) are then analyzed using the Peres lattice structure.
model_or_system: The study focuses on periodically driven quantum systems, exemplified by a Lipkin–Meshkov–Glick type model involving collective spin operators ($\hat{J}_x, \hat{J}_z$). The dynamics are governed by a time-dependent Hamiltonian $\hat{H}(t) = \hat{H}_0 + \eta g(t) \hat{H}'$.
key_observables: Peres lattice coordinates (expectation values of observables), Floquet quasienergies, and the similarity measure $N$ comparing driven vs. stationary dynamics.
important_parameters: Driving strength ($\eta$), time period ($T$), system size parameter ($j$), and critical coupling constants ($\kappa_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximating the full Floquet evolution operator using truncated expansions (e.g., BCH or Dyson series) to construct effective stationary Hamiltonians.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Peres lattices for both stationary and kicked systems, showing structural changes corresponding to resonances and chaos onset; they also compare Husimi distributions derived from different driving forms.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the applicability of Peres lattices to driven systems, then analyzing quantum phase transitions in the stationary limit, followed by detailed investigations into resonance detection, chaos growth, and comparisons between various continuous and kicked driving protocols using approximation techniques.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, geometric diagnostic tool (Peres lattices) to visualize complex phenomena like chaos and resonances in time-dependent quantum systems, bridging the gap between static and driven many-body physics relevant to cavity QED or ultracold atoms.
